title: Data Disclosure
description: Parent User (EE1) shares personal data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) with the Authentication Service (P1) via the registration flow. This act of sharing causes a privacy threat because the data is exposed to an untrusted third party.
assumptions: The parent user is aware of the data sharing and intends to proceed with registration.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Personal data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) is transmitted between the Parent User (EE1) and the Authentication Service (P1) via the data flow (DF1). This data-centric threat arises because the data is exposed during transmission, potentially allowing interception or linking of the user to their credentials.
assumptions: The transmission is secure, but the data itself is inherently exposed in transit.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The Authentication Service (P1) receives the user's data and processes it for authentication purposes. This processing action causes a privacy threat because the service may use the data in ways not authorized by the user (e.g., storing it, using it for other services, or disclosing it to third parties during authentication).
assumptions: The service processes the data for authentication as intended.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Authentication Service (Process P1) shares parent account data with the MongoDB users collection (DataStore DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The MongoDB users collection (DataStore DS1) receives and stores the parent account data. The minimality principle is violated if the store is not restricted to storing strictly required personal data.

title: Unauthorized Access to JWT
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT tokens with the parent user (ExternalEntity EE1). If the parent user is not properly authenticated or if the JWT is compromised, an unauthorized party could access the protected user data.
assumptions: The parent user is not verified before receiving the JWT.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data-centric threat arises at the data flow (DF3). The JWT and user data are transmitted in transit. If the transmission channel is intercepted, the data could be read by an eavesdropper before reaching the destination.
assumptions: The network is not encrypted or uses a weak protocol.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (ExternalEntity EE1) receives the JWT and user data. If the parent user is not properly authenticated, the parent entity could process or store the data in a way that causes a privacy threat.
assumptions: The parent user is not verified before processing the data.

title: Unencrypted Credentials
description: Child User (EE2) shares login credentials (email, password) with Authentication Service (P1) without encryption, exposing sensitive data in transit.

title: Data in Transit
description: Credentials are transmitted via unencrypted channel (DF4), allowing interception by third parties.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: Authentication Service (P1) processes and stores the credentials, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the child user's account.

title: JWT Issuance
description: The source element (Process P1) generates a JWT containing user type information. This act of sharing the JWT with the child element (ExternalEntity EE2) exposes the user's identity and attributes to the external system, creating a privacy risk.
assumptions: The JWT is not encrypted or tokenized before transmission.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data-centric threat arises at the data flow (DF5). The JWT payload, which contains sensitive user type information, is transmitted in plaintext or unencrypted format between the Process and the ExternalEntity. This allows an attacker to intercept the data and potentially link or identify the user.
assumptions: No encryption or tokenization is applied to the JWT during transmission.

title: Data Processing
description: The destination element (ExternalEntity EE2) receives the JWT and processes it. The external system may store, use, or display the user type information without proper validation or masking, leading to potential privacy breaches.
assumptions: The external system does not validate the JWT's authenticity or restrict access to the user type field.

title: Profile Linking via Recurring Attributes
description: The external entity (EE1) shares a child profile containing quasi-identifiers (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) with the process (P3). This combination of attributes allows the process to link and identify the individual, enabling the creation of a user profile that can be used for targeted data collection or profiling.
assumptions: The process (P3) is configured to store and potentially use this profile for future interactions.

title: Data-Centric Linking in Transit
description: The data flow (DF6) transmits the profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) between the external entity and the process. The meta-data about the parties involved (EE1 and P3) and the specific attributes being shared can be used to link or identify the data subject, facilitating the creation of a profile.
assumptions: The data is transmitted in a format that allows for identification or linking.

title: Child Profile Disclosure
description: Process P3 shares child profile data (id P3) with DataStore DS2 (id DS2) for storage. This constitutes a data disclosure (D) as the process transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store, potentially violating the minimality principle if not strictly required.
assumptions: Child profile data is considered personal data under LINDDUN Pro.
uncertainty_note: Assuming child profiles contain identifiable personal information.

title: Child Profile Storage/Processing
description: DataStore DS2 receives and stores the child profile data. Processing or storing data in a way that causes a threat, such as making it accessible to unauthorized parties or for purposes beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: DS2 stores the data for child profile management purposes.
uncertainty_note: Assuming DS2's storage actions are not strictly necessary for the child profile's intended functionality.

title: Unauthorized Video Search
description: External entity EE2 (Child User) initiates a video search request without explicit authorization or consent, potentially exposing sensitive video content.
assumptions: User has not been granted specific permissions for this data flow.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: Data-centric threat: The metadata associated with the video search request (e.g., user ID, search query) may be used to link or identify the external entity EE2, facilitating unauthorized access.
assumptions: Metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Destination element P2 (Video Management Service) processes or stores the video search data in a way that causes a threat, potentially violating privacy policies or data retention rules.
assumptions: Recipient processes or stores data in a way that causes the threat.

title: Identified Information in Metadata
description: The video metadata (e.g., file names, sizes, timestamps) shared by the Process at the source element (P2) contains identified information (e.g., specific video IDs, user identifiers, or other personally identifiable information). This constitutes a Data Disclosure threat (D) at the source, as the transfer of this metadata to the DataStore (DS3) facilitates the identification of the data recipients or the data itself.

title: Data Disclosure via Meta-data
description: The data flow (DF9) itself transmits video metadata (e.g., file names, sizes, timestamps) to the destination (DS3). This constitutes a Data Disclosure (Dd) threat at the data flow, as the transfer of this metadata to the DataStore (DS3) facilitates the identification of the data recipients or the data itself.

title: Identified Information in Metadata
description: The DataStore (DS3) receives the video metadata and stores it. The storage of this metadata (e.g., file names, sizes, timestamps) constitutes a Data Disclosure (D) threat at the destination, as the storage of this metadata facilitates the identification of the data recipients or the data itself.

title: Child Search History Disclosure
description: Process P3 (Child Profile Management) shares its data (child search and watch history) with DataStore DS2 (MongoDB childprofiles collection). This constitutes a data disclosure (D) as the process transfers personal data across a boundary to a third party (the database).

title: Meta-Data Disclosure
description: Data flow DF10 transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., process identifiers, data types, or access patterns) to the data store. This is a data disclosure (Dd) threat, as the transfer of metadata can be used to identify or link the data entities.

title: Child Search History Storage
description: DataStore DS2 receives the child search and watch history data and stores it. The act of storing this personal data in a database creates a potential for future disclosure or unauthorized access, as the data is now under the control of the system.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Data
description: External entity (EE1) shares video data with the Video Management Service (P2) without proper authentication or authorization controls. This allows unauthorized users to access sensitive video content.
assumptions: No authentication mechanism is in place for the data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the system has any form of access control or logging for the data sharing event.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow DF11 transmits video data along with metadata identifying the uploader (EE1) and the service (P2). This metadata can be used to link or identify the parties involved, potentially enabling targeted surveillance or data profiling.
assumptions: The metadata includes identifiers that could be used for identification.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard metadata includes user identifiers.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service (P2) processes the uploaded video data in a way that may lead to improper personal data management. This could include storing, processing, or sharing the data in a manner that violates privacy principles or regulations.
assumptions: The service's processing of the video data does not include appropriate safeguards for personal data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the service has implemented appropriate safeguards for personal data.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The process (P2) shares video data with an external entity (EE2). This interaction is invalid under the mapping table, as external entities do not have modeled flows between each other. The sharing of video data with an external entity without a defined process interaction creates a privacy risk related to improper personal data management.
assumptions: The video data is considered personal data.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The data flow (DF12) carries video data between the process (P2) and the external entity (EE2). The invalid interaction (ExternalEntity -> Process) implies that the data in transit is being used to link or identify the parties, which is a data-centric threat related to improper personal data management.
assumptions: The video data contains identifying or linking information.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The destination element (EE2) receives the video data. The invalid interaction implies that the external entity is processing or storing the data in a way that causes a privacy threat, specifically related to improper personal data management.
assumptions: The external entity is processing the video data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The child browsing data (personal data) is transferred from the DataStore (DS2) to the AI Recommendation Engine (P4). This constitutes a data disclosure as the data is shared across a boundary to a third party (the AI engine).
assumptions: The data transfer is intentional and designed as part of the child browsing functionality.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Meta-data about the parties involved in the data flow (e.g., the identity of the child and the AI engine) is transmitted during transit. This metadata can be used to link or identify the data recipients, constituting a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata that could be used for identification.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) receives the data and processes it in a way that causes the threat. The engine may store or use the data for its recommendation functions, which could involve processing personal data.
assumptions: The AI engine processes the received data for its recommendation functionality.

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (Process P4) shares browsing data with Third-Party Advertisers (ExternalEntity EE3). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers personal data to a known third party, potentially violating the minimality principle if not strictly required.
assumptions: The data transfer is planned and intended.

title: Data Disclosure via Meta-Data
description: Data-centric threats at the data flow (fl) involve meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them. The flow between P4 and EE3 may carry metadata that facilitates the identification of the data subjects, even if the actual data transfer is not the primary concern.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata that could be used to identify the parties.
uncertainty_note: Confident that metadata about the parties is present in the data flow.

title: Data Disclosure by Third-Party Advertiser
description: At the destination (EE3), the Third-Party Advertiser receives and processes the browsing data. This action constitutes a data disclosure as the external entity processes the data, potentially violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: The advertiser processes the data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The process P1 shares government ID images (personal data) with the data store DS4. This constitutes a data disclosure as the transfer of personal data across a boundary (from the process to the data store).

title: Data-centric Threat
description: Data-centric threats such as meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them. The flow DF15 carries metadata about the data flow itself, which could be used to identify the parties involved.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store DS4 receives the government ID images and processes or stores them. This action of storing personal data in a way that causes a threat constitutes a data disclosure.

title: Unauthorized Access to JWT
description: The source element (Process P1) shares a JWT (JSON Web Token) in localStorage. If the JWT is compromised or if the process is triggered to retransmit it, the act of sharing causes a privacy threat. This is a data-centric threat where the act of sharing itself is the vector for potential exposure.
assumptions: The JWT is stored in localStorage and is being accessed or retransmitted by the Process.

title: Data in Transit (Meta-data)
description: The data flow (DF16) carries the JWT in transit. A data-centric threat arises here if meta-data about the JWT (e.g., its size, timestamp, or content hash) is used to link or identify the parties involved in the flow, potentially enabling tracking or correlation.
assumptions: The JWT is being transmitted between the Process and the DataStore.

title: Unauthorized Processing/Storage
description: The destination element (DataStore DS5) receives the JWT. If the data is processed or stored in a way that causes a privacy threat (e.g., being used to identify the user, or if the storage mechanism is insecure), a threat arises at the destination.
assumptions: The JWT is stored in DS5 and is being accessed or processed by the DataStore.

title: Profile Linking
description: Process P3 (Child Profile Management) shares data with ExternalEntity EE1 (Parent User). The process retrieves child history and associates it with the parent's identity. This linkage, potentially using recurring identifiers or quasi-identifiers common to the child profile, allows the parent to build a profile of the child, revealing additional information about the child's privacy.
assumptions: The child profile contains sufficient identifying or quasi-identifying information to be linked to the parent's identity.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the child profile contains enough quasi-identifiers to be linked to the parent's identity; depends on the specific attributes stored in P3.

title: Linking in Transit
description: The data flow DF17 carries child profile data between P3 and EE1. The act of transmitting this data, potentially including metadata about the parties involved (e.g., 'Child Profile Management' and 'Parent User'), facilitates the linking of the child's data to the parent's identity.
assumptions: The metadata associated with the data flow (e.g., entity names) is used to identify the parties.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the metadata used to identify the parties is sufficient for linking purposes.

title: Data Processing
description: At the destination (EE1), the parent user receives the child profile data. The processing of this data by the parent may involve storing or using it in a way that enables the parent to build a profile of the child, thereby revealing additional information about the child's privacy.
assumptions: The parent user processes the received data in a way that allows for profile building.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent's processing of the data leads to profile building.
